notice: These are newly derived, unvalidated educational observations. The source supplies no printed answer key for this exercise. They are unscored and require qualified ECG educator review.

fields.basis: Assumed course speed 25 mm/s; 151 grid lines enclose 150 small horizontal intervals across 1161 pixels.
fields.reason: 6 retained positive peak-to-peak intervals have mean spacing 144.75 px, giving 80.2 bpm. Individual-interval estimates span approximately 66.5–96.8 bpm under the same assumption; this is observed interval variation, not a confidence interval. No numerical speed label or labeled timing duration is verified on this strip. This is interval-derived, not a six-second beat count or a claim of a stable rate.

fields.value: Candidate P-wave observation: Four smooth low-amplitude positive pre-complex humps recur. Their leading edges are shallow and blend with baseline drift; identity and exact onset remain less secure than the larger candidates on page 444. One low-amplitude candidate is visible before each of the four selected sharp complexes, but separation of the candidate tail from the initial negative notch is not secure.

fields.value: Ventricular intervals progressively shorten; the conditional mean-interval estimate is about 80 bpm and is not a stable rate. Small pre-complex lobes recur, but atrial identity and PR/QRS boundaries remain unresolved. Sinus arrhythmia cannot be selected without confirming sinus-compatible P morphology, the atrial-to-ventricular sequence and PR behavior throughout; the present strip has no accepted numeric PR or QRS field.

fields.reason: No diagnostic rhythm label, validated P-wave identity, conduction interval or clinical conclusion is assigned. Qualified ECG educator review has not occurred. limitations: Wave observations and conditional endpoint envelopes remain provisional and unscored. QT/QTc, calibrated amplitudes and clinical diagnosis are not established. Selected-complex widths do not establish sequence certainty.

pr unresolved: Independent reviewer could bracket an exploratory range, but author raises this unresolved component-boundary issue: Tiny/shallow preceding candidates and/or competing ventricular onset choices prevent a uniquely supported PR field. The manual endpoint scenarios are retained, not silently converted to PR. Preserve both positions; this is not proof of irreducible unmeasurability.

qrs unresolved: Independent reviewer could bracket an exploratory range, but author raises this unresolved component-boundary issue: Terminal recovery merges into a continuing sloping contour without a uniquely resolved QRS-ST junction. Both shoulder choices remain scenarios. Preserve both positions; this is not proof of irreducible unmeasurability.

The current review provides provisional measurements, descriptive morphology and conditional educational comparisons. It does not assign a clinical diagnosis or a validated rhythm label.
Seven complete interior deflections are used. Neither visible edge fragment is treated as a complete extra beat.

The 150-small-interval span would be six seconds only under the assumed course convention. Unlabeled top marks do not independently verify that duration. Only measured horizontal spacing is used for time, not vertical pixel spacing.

Approximate ±2 source pixels per fiducial and ±0.15 pixels per grid pitch are illustrative sensitivity allowances, not confidence limits. They exclude unknown speed, source distortion and incorrect waveform identification.
A mean rate can conceal changing spacing. Read the regularity description and individual-interval range; no sustained rate or diagnostic rhythm is inferred.

Both separated waveform-free bands yield the same continuous sequence; local thirds corroborate pitch. Counts are measured, not inherited from another batch. Lower thresholds can create 3 px spurious split groups; higher thresholds can drop faint lines and create 15–24 px gaps. Selected thresholds retain a coherent sequence in both bands without interpolation.
Left-edge ventricular deflection is partly clipped; its onset/apex cannot be established completely, so it and adjacent edge interval are excluded.
Right-edge rising deflection is truncated before a complete apex/return; excluded from fiducial and interval measurements.

measurementEvidence.landmarkType: Upper extremum of each manually identified complete steep upright ventricular component; median x among darkest apex-row pixels.
measurementEvidence.rateMethod: 60 / (mean ventricular-fiducial interval pixels * 0.04 / pixels per small square)
